articles.title: High Court Rules Against Ownership Claim for Hopwood Hall
articles.excerpt: The High Court has ruled that Rochdale Council acted fairly in its decision not to transfer ownership of Hopwood Hall to Hopwood DePree, a descendant of the original owners.
articles.content_html:
A High Court in Manchester has ruled that Rochdale Council did not act unfairly in its decision not to transfer ownership of Hopwood Hall to Hopwood DePree, a descendant of the family that originally built the hall in the 1420s. The ruling concluded a two-day trial concerning an exclusivity agreement that had been established for the sale of the historic Grade II-listed property.

Mr DePree, who took legal action against the council, expressed disappointment with the outcome, stating it was a significant setback for both his family and the community. He indicated that his team is currently exploring legal options for potential next steps. Mr DePree emphasised the importance of Hopwood Hall to the community and its historical significance, urging the council to focus on restoring the property for public benefit.

Hopwood Hall has a rich history, having been owned by the Hopwood family until 1922, after which it changed hands multiple times. It was used as a Catholic teacher training college until the 1980s and has since fallen into disrepair. Rochdale Council acquired the property and is responsible for its maintenance and future development.

The ruling may impact future plans for the restoration and use of Hopwood Hall, as the council continues to seek ways to preserve the site for community use. The next steps for both the council and Mr DePree remain to be seen as discussions about the hall's future continue.
